statements.venue: Written candidate questionnaire answer (Iowa governor race)
statements.quote: Artificial intelligence needs commonsense, enforceable guardrails that defend the rights and privacy of Iowans, protect jobs in Iowa, and support economic growth, innovation, and the entrepreneurial spirit.
statements.context: Technology Association of Iowa asked gubernatorial candidates for their views on Iowa's innovation economy, including AI.
statements.reason: Calls for AI guardrails for privacy, jobs and growth, but names no catastrophic risk.

grade_reason: His only 2026 statement on AI found calls for guardrails on privacy, jobs and growth without acknowledging catastrophic risk. Nothing at level A, B, C or F was found.
notes: Eight web searches ran, all returned results. The statement date is the page's published_time metadata (2026-04-17); the page itself shows no date, and it says only that candidates submitted responses, so the answer may have been written by campaign staff. Feenstra was a 2026 candidate for Iowa governor; one search result described Zach Lahn as the Republican nominee, which I did not verify. Search results found no sign that Feenstra co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, lead sponsor Rep. Greg Casar), whose named cosponsors are Democrats, but I did not open the congress.gov cosponsor list. His official press release index (latest July 2026) showed no AI releases in its excerpts. Older AI activity outside the window: the Farm Tech Act (December 2023, AI software certification for agriculture, based on the NIST risk management framework) and a September 2022 Science Committee hearing statement on managing AI risks; not graded because they predate 2025.
